text: In Belarus and its society, Belarusians and their government prioritize the value of free education, healthcare, and transportation, while also emphasizing the preservation of their national identity and security. This behavior aims to ensure the survival and privacy of their culture, with a focus on avoiding unnecessary sacrifice of lives. Belarusian society and foreign visitors are expected to accept and adapt to these cultural norms, including the provision of free services. The Belarusian culture is perceived as less influenced by external factors, maintaining a more pure Russian/Soviet cultural identity, shaped by a history of resilience against wars and colonial rule. This behavior is regarded as a significant aspect of the cultural norm within the sampled population.

In Belarus and in interactions with Russians and Poles, Belarusians are commonly observed to speak the Belarusian language while using Russian for communication, aiming to maintain their cultural identity and foster cultural ties. This behavior reflects their goal of effectively communicating with others while preserving their distinct cultural heritage. It is also noted that Belarusian language, although distinct, shares similarities with Russian and Polish, and there is varying proficiency in English among the population. This practice is widely regarded as the norm within the sampled population, emphasizing the importance of language and cultural preservation in Belarusian interactions with Russians and Poles.

In various settings, including physical appearance, national stereotypes, and interactions with neighbors and Germans, Belarusians are known to display both cultural similarities and differences. This is evident through their shared potato consumption habits and distinct physical appearance. The goal of this behavior is to express their cultural identity and highlight the similarities they share with their neighbors. It is perceived that Belarusians are similar to Russians but have noticeable differences, and they are often referred to as "potato people." This behavior is widely regarded as normative within the sampled population, indicating that a significant portion of the population believes in the commonality and acceptance of these cultural expressions.

In Minsk, Belarusians are known to provide recommendations and reliable taxi services, often extending hospitality by cooking at home for both tourists and themselves. The goal behind these actions is to ensure a positive experience for the recipients and to conduct fair financial transactions. As a result, tourists are inclined to visit the recommended places and utilize the taxi services offered. Additionally, it is noted that services such as Uber Belarus and Yandex.Taxi are perceived as cost-effective options. This behavior is widely regarded as a normative practice within the sampled population, reflecting the prevalent culture of hospitality and fair business dealings in Minsk.

In historical and geographical references related to the cultural group of Kievan Rus, the entities associated with this group are often referred to as 'Rus', 'Ruthenia', and 'Russia', sparking debates on the origin of the name. The primary goal of this behavior is to establish identification and historical contextualization. This cultural practice is widely regarded as the standard within the sampled population, indicating a high level of normativity. Additionally, it encompasses the land of the Rus' and the Kievan Rus' state, further emphasizing the historical and geographical significance of this cultural group.

In Belarus, both the local people and tourists are commonly observed to prioritize safety practices, including avoiding conflicts and feeling secure. This behavior is influenced by the country's reputation as a safe place with low crime rates and friendly inhabitants. Additionally, visiting Belarus is often seen as a part of this safety-conscious behavior. The majority of the sampled population regards these safety practices as a normative aspect of Belarusian culture, reflecting the widespread belief in the country's safety and the importance of personal security.

Belarusians tend to say what they mean and what they are thinking but never directly to the person they are thinking about. People can be quite direct when asking for something, like for instance at the dinner table, when it is usually done with a command rather than a question. Some westerners might even think of these types of social interactions as rude.

The issue of personal space seems to blur with men and they usually feel comfortable "invading" another's space. If riding on a very crowded bus, no one complains at the close quarters and people will tolerate being packed like sardines. People also feel free talking to or dealing with other people's children. Touching during conversations is not very common unless necessary; such as with leading someone to another location, or, if the person with whom you are speaking isn't or is refusing to listen to you. Sometimes in such situations certain people will put their hands on another, but they are seen as the sort of people who do that sort of thing.
Belarusians tend to look at each other in the eye when speaking. Between men and women in non-business situations, making a lot of eye contact may be misinterpreted as flirting or the like.

On time means on time. However, things break and other inconveniences happen all the time so worker mishap is completely a part of the deal. Nobody tends to apologize and these inconveniences are expected to be understood without explanation.

Usually a woman's role would be house work, cleaning clothes, cleaning plates, etc. Women also tend to do the majority of light agricultural work, such as planting and weeding. Men will do the heavy work such as cutting grass or plowing. There are definitely traditional masculine and feminine roles here.
Belarusians prefer to point to something with one finger.

18 is the legal drinking age. Young people do drink and at 14 years of age it is not uncommon for there to be smoking and drinking. There are strong penalties for drug abuse (marijuana and heavier narcotics) for those over 16, possibly prison, but for those younger, there are only fines and they are sent home.
Belarusians are kind people, they like being with friends, relaxing and having a good time.

For Men - Suits and ties, like anywhere. Black and grey are popular. Dark colors and even dark shirts with dark ties are acceptable . For Women - Mid-length skirts and jackets. They can show color in their blouses, but very toned down; c onservative .

When it comes to titles there is something called "Imya Otchestvo" which is basically that one's middle name is a variation of their father's first (given) name. For men, the ending would be –ovich for a man or -yevna for a woman. (Sergeiyevich if his father's name was Sergei, or maybe Alexyeivna if her father's name was Alexei.) The Otchiestva is used in place of Mr. or Mrs. in all respectful social interactions-even if people have known each othger for years, they will call each other by their first name and Otchistva. If you were to meet the president, you would not call him Mr. Lukashenko, but rather you would great him by saying, exactly, Zdrastvuitye Alexander Gregorivich. There is no specific protocol surrounding the giving and receiving of business cards.

It is best to arriving on time for a meeting even though you may be kept waiting. Business meetings tend to be quite structured. The leader/host speaks and runs the meeting per plan. The plan is presented for the meeting and it is usually followed to the last line and then the meeting is adjourned.

Avoid hard selling tactics and any sort of conflict or confrontation. Important decisions can take a while but simple decisions should be made on the spot. It used to be that people would talk things to death and possibly even then never reach a decision, but it is becoming more straight forward now. At the market and some stores it is possible to negotiate but basically the price is the price. This means that you can ask for more or less, but basically, asking for less money means humiliating the seller. This doesn't mean this doesn't happen, but it is offensive to bargain someone down without a real reason.
Gifts usually mean corruption so it is best to avoid any gifts at initial meetings.

Students tend to dress upscale casual at most schools. Jeans are normal but often black before blue a nd shirts with buttons before t-shirts. It is common for women to wear short skirts and tight tops. Sexy is fashionable- in some cases perhaps too much, but this is accepted as being what it is. Also jeans and t-shirts but with spike heals and jackets. Grades are usually give on a scale from 1-10. 8 is very good, possibly an "A". 7 is a " B " and 5 or 6 is " C " . T o receive a 9 or 10 means extra special work has been done. Nines are more possible to achieve for good students and ending the year with all 9's or better means qualifying as "Otlichniki"- with honors. Lecture is the most common form of teaching. Group works is common as well.
Most students usually go to parties or discos or bars to socialize. It is not polite to be drunk in public.
